answer: In PoA, trust propagates as a bounded-length random walk on the attestation graph, initialized by a beacon and damped at each step. A sybil coalition concentrated behind a sparse external cut has low conductance, so few walk transitions enter it; conductance and min-cut transitivity bounds cap its stationary mass and thus aggregate voting weight, even when its internal trellis is dense. The bound holds below the honest zenith of connectivity.
